claims.statement: The fragment describes enterprise-owner setup of Business or Enterprise subscriptions, directing credit-card/PayPal purchasers to a purchase link and other payment methods to Sales. Its included trial note requires paid-enterprise conversion before purchase from an Enterprise Cloud trial. These historical owner capabilities and links are not cost approval, permission to contact Sales, actual purchase, or reviewed payment terms.

The organization fragment describes Business purchase by owners of Free or Team organizations and, for enterprise-owned organizations whose enterprise subscribes, asking the enterprise owner to enable access through the personal Copilot settings request route. Purchase capability, access request, enterprise enablement, and granted seats are distinct; none was performed or approved here.

The example presents a .github-private/copilot layout with managed-settings.json specifying an overridable auto model, team-mappings.json assigning no-auto.json to special-team, and teams/no-auto.json specifying an unmanaged model. Filename variables were resolved at the pin. This expected illustrative tree does not establish parser precedence, team identity resolution, valid deployed configuration, or effective enforcement; no example files were installed.

The preview fragment attributes access control to organization and enterprise policies and links specifically to enterprise-cloud policy sections for previews or feedback. It neither establishes a selected policy value nor universal preview support, user eligibility, or authorization to enable a preview; destinations are not newly reviewed by this receipt.

The prompt-files fragment limits its described availability to VS Code, Visual Studio, and JetBrains IDEs. This pinned surface list is not a current feature matrix, verified file application, or assurance that imported prompts are safe to follow.

The further-reading fragment links VS Code prompt-file creation/use documentation, Copilot response-customization concepts, and community-contributed prompt/customization material on a moving main-branch link. These pointers are not destination review, license clearance, trusted instructions, tested functionality, or policy adoption.
